Guiding Claude (Opus 5.5), I've had Claude create a Lean4 proof that formalizes Itai, Papadimitriou and Swarcfiter's 1982 paper "Hamilton Paths in Grid Graphs" (10.113/0211056) "acceptability iff Hamiltonian path" condition. That is, for a rectangle of specified width, height, start and end point, an instance is "acceptable" iff it has a Hamiltonian path from s to t within the rectangle.

I've made a GitHub repo which can be found at zzyzek/GridHam2D-Lean. The project compiles with Lean's three standard axioms and, for me, with no warnings. My version information in case it's useful:

Lean (version 4.35.0-rc2, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, commit 11acb17ec6b07a8f9e9173e6845197929540936b, Release)

I asked Claude to create a Lean4 proof to get more familiarity with the process as well as a hope that I could use it for future proofs. I'm not sure if others will find it useful but I thought I would announce it here in case anyone was interested. I am, otherwise, a complete beginner regarding my ability to program in Lean.

Any advice on how to structure the project, whether it should be submitted elsewhere or other constructive criticism would be welcome.

I am working on a tool to convert English requirements into a checkable specification. I use Lean as the language that is checked for a formal grammar. What allows this is that you can launch a web server in Lean4, to make it an actor that you can talk to over http.

https://rfielding.github.io/leanFM.pdf
